Which traditions would you most like to learn — or help teach?

Tick as many as you like. There is no limit, and choosing something does not commit you to anything.

Some of these are practical workshops; some touch on prayer and the life of the Church. Where a topic calls for authoritative teaching, Father would lead or approve it — what that means is set out below.

Bread, food and the feasts

The kitchen is where a great deal of this has always been handed on.

Prosphora appears here as a class to attend. What happens after the class — the bread offered for the Divine Liturgy, and how a baker joins the parish's rotation — is set out under Bake the bread on Get Involved.

Prosphora baking

Learn how prosphora is prepared and stamped for use in the Divine Liturgy.

Reported: the parish already offers this class.

Making koliva

Learn how to prepare and decorate koliva, and about its connection to Orthodox memorial traditions and the hope of the Resurrection.

Artoklasia bread

Learn about the five loaves used in the Artoklasia service and how they are prepared.

Vasilopita

Learn how to prepare Vasilopita, and about the tradition of St. Basil and the hidden coin.

Best kept near the New Year

Fanouropita

Learn about the tradition associated with St. Phanourios, and how Fanouropita is prepared.

Lazarakia

Learn to make the traditional Lazarus-shaped breads associated with Lazarus Saturday.

Best kept before Palm Sunday

Traditional Pascha eggs

Learn how to prepare traditional red Pascha eggs, and the symbolism and customs that go with them.

Best kept in Holy Week

Traditional Lenten cooking

Learn recipes and practical food traditions associated with the fasting seasons of the Church.

Holy Week and Pascha

The week the whole parish prepares for together.

Palm cross folding

Learn how to fold traditional palm crosses for Palm Sunday.

Good for adults, teens and families

Holy Week preparations

A hands-on workshop on the traditions connected with Palm Sunday, Holy Week and Pascha.

Kouvouklion — Holy Friday flowers

Learn about the tradition of decorating the Kouvouklion with flowers, and how parishioners can help prepare it.

Great Lent at home

Practical traditions that help a family enter more deeply into Great Lent.

Holy Week and Pascha at home

Ways families can prepare their homes, and their children, for Holy Week and Pascha.

The Church year at home

What the parish does on Sunday, kept through the week in the house.

Building a home prayer corner

Practical ways Orthodox Christians arrange and use icons, prayer books, candles, incense, holy water and other devotional items at home.

Any theological or pastoral guidance would be under Father’s direction.

Incense at home

Learn about incense, how to light charcoal safely, and how incense may be used appropriately in Orthodox prayer at home.

Would be offered only with Father’s approval.

Name day traditions

How Orthodox Christians celebrate patron saints and name days, at home and in the life of the parish.

Feast days in the home

Simple ways families can bring the Church year into the home through prayer, food, icons, decorations and traditions.

Nativity and Theophany traditions

A seasonal workshop on the traditions connected with the Nativity of Christ and Theophany.

Worship, words and prayer

Things that make Sunday morning easier to follow, and prayer easier to keep.

The responses of the Divine Liturgy

A practical session to help parishioners learn the common responses and take part in worship more confidently.

Greek words you hear every Sunday

A friendly introduction to the Greek liturgical words and phrases heard regularly at The Nativity — Kyrie eleison, Sophia, Proschomen, Eirene pasi, Doxa Patri, and others.

Prayer rope knotting

How traditional prayer ropes are made, and about the Jesus Prayer.

Would be offered only if someone qualified is available to teach it.

Handwork and remembrance

Skills that are quietly held by a few people and easily lost.

Iconography demonstration

A qualified Orthodox iconographer demonstrates the process and explains the materials, the symbolism and the theology of iconography.

A demonstration by an iconographer — not a paint-your-own-icon craft session.

Traditional Orthodox handwork

A flexible category for parishioners who know embroidery, church sewing, liturgical textile work, candle making or other traditional handcrafts.

Orthodox memorial and funeral traditions

An adult workshop explaining the practical parish traditions surrounding death, memorials, koliva and remembrance.

Father would lead or approve the pastoral and theological portions.
